newsitem.title: USA: IMF board members cautiously welcome Ukraine plans.
newsitem.headline: IMF board members cautiously welcome Ukraine plans.

text.p: IMF board members cautiously welcomed Ukraine's ambitious economic reform program at an informal meeting on Wednesday, monetary sources said.

The gathering, at which IMF staff presented the results of recent negotiations with Kiev, was a prelude to a formal meeting of the International Monetary Fund board tentatively set for Dec. 12 for an in-depth discussion of Ukraine's plans.
At that meeting, the board is expected to approve the final $210 million tranche of a $867 million stand-by loan for Ukraine, the sources, who declined to be named, said.

It is also expected to discuss Ukraine's plans to further restructure its economy, although it will delay approval of a new $2.5 to $3.0 billion, three-year loan for the country until its Parliament has approved the reform plans, they said.
"It's quite an ambitious program," an international monetary source said, adding that it received a good reception at Wednesday's informal IMF board gathering.
Much of the reforms, which range from restructuring of the agriculture sector to sharp tightening of budget policy, will be front-loaded and carried out early in the program.
